A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FoGE and FoGE-LLM. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, references, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original graph-understanding, molecular and protein benchmark results, graph-prompting experiments, reconstruction analyses, dimensionality ablations, and inference timings.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds measurements of FoGE encoding runtime across increasing graph sizes in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The implemented encoding remains unchanged: random or text-encoded vectors, circular-convolution binding, additive aggregation, graph-size encoding, and the attribute and hypergraph constructions in Equations (1)–(4). FoGE-LLM still uses linear adapters with a frozen LLM. The revised mathematical motivation does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: v2 adds an explicit large-graph encoding scenario using random Erdos-Renyi graphs with up to five million edges in Appendix E. Downstream dataset and task coverage is retained; mol-HIV and the basic graph-understanding experiments were already evaluated in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods, including GraphToken, GraphLLM, zero/few-shot prompting, and the molecular and biomedical baselines. The new encoding-runtime experiment evaluates FoGE alone. Newly cited LLaVA and Time-LLM works are contextual references, not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: New Appendix E introduces a CPU timing protocol varying edge counts across 1, 500, 50,000, 1,200,000, and 5,000,000. Existing training settings, metrics, and inference comparisons remain unchanged. The newly stated mol-HIV scaffold split documents an existing experiment rather than establishing a changed split.

E4.justification: v2 adds a scaling analysis testing how encoding runtime changes with graph edge count. The capacity/reconstruction analyses, SabDab clade visualization, and vector-dimensionality ablation remain unchanged. Moving basic-task and mol-HIV results into the main text does not introduce additional analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report uncertainty using the same unexplained plus/minus convention for mol-HIV results and inference timings. The new runtime table extends this practice without specifying run counts, seeds, or a new estimation procedure. No confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: v2 Table 10 adds encoding times, including 94.041 ± 1.04 seconds for 1.2 million edges and 378.018 ± 4.55 seconds for five million edges. Matched benchmark scores, reconstruction and dimensionality findings, and LLM inference timings are unchanged; relocated tables do not demonstrate performance improvements.

T1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.2 substantially revise the mathematical construction. v2 corrects T(W) from exterior algebra to tensor algebra and explicitly derives anticommutation. It replaces v1's spectral-square-root Dirac construction and coefficient-matrix anticommutation assertion with a Hodge-Laplacian formulation, abstract Clifford generators, and graded creation/annihilation operations. This changes the formal rationale without adding a proof of the implemented encoder's guarantees.

C1.justification: The theoretical-origin claim is narrowed: the abstract drops the assertion that the construction is inherited directly from theory, and the conclusion replaces rigorous Clifford/Fock grounding with Fock-space motivation. The central claims about parameter-free encoding, frozen-LLM prompting, and applicability across graph types remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds reasons for using an LLM, including a flexible language interface and integration with existing software ecosystems, and interprets graph grounding through analogies with LLaVA and Time-LLM. Appendix E discusses scalability and possible CPU parallelization. Existing limitations concerning fixed embeddings and text-encoder compatibility are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly describes mol-HIV's prediction target, nine-dimensional atom features, and scaffold splits. The code pointer changes from an anonymous repository to the named SPChytas/FoGE GitHub repository. Conversely, the explicit source identifying the molecular-fingerprint method is removed. Existing adapter-training details are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds mathematical references supporting the revised exposition, acknowledges the authors' earlier graph-encoding workshop paper, and introduces ReCO, LLaVA, and Time-LLM citations. It removes the extended-connectivity fingerprint reference. These expand attribution and contextual positioning without replacing the main comparison with existing graph-prompting research.

P1.justification: The Clifford/Dirac/Fock exposition is substantially rewritten, and the experimental narrative is reorganized to incorporate previously appendix-only basic-task and mol-HIV material. v2 adds a main-text inference-runtime subsection and replaces the former Appendix E organization with encoding-runtime analysis. These changes exceed routine copyediting.

P2.justification: The empirical displays are substantially reorganized: v1's appendix Tables 7–8 become main-text Tables 1–2, inference timings appear in both the main text and appendix, and a new encoding-runtime table is added. Existing result tables are resized and reflowed, with corrected best-score emphasis in the GraphQA table. The nine numbered figures retain their visual contents.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the tensor-algebra definition, clarifies the theoretical exposition, and makes existing empirical evidence easier to inspect. New CPU scaling measurements and fuller mol-HIV documentation provide modest additional support. These benefits outweigh the loss of the fingerprint-method citation, although runtime hardware and repetition details remain unspecified and the revised theory still does not establish the encoder's claimed guarantees.
